notes.summary: Measures of central tendency give one value that represents the whole data: arithmetic mean, median, mode, geometric mean and harmonic mean. JSO asks direct computations (raw and grouped data), the empirical relation, and properties.

concepts.title: The means
concepts.body:
• Arithmetic mean x̄ = Σx/n (raw), Σfx/Σf (grouped, using class marks).
  • Combined mean = (n1x̄1 + n2x̄2)/(n1 + n2).
  • Geometric mean = (x1x2…xn)1/n; used for ratios and growth rates.
  • Harmonic mean = n / Σ(1/x); used for average speed over equal distances.
  • For positive values: AM ≥ GM ≥ HM, and for two numbers GM² = AM × HM.

concepts.title: Median and mode
concepts.body:
• Median: middle value after sorting. For even n, the average of the two middle values.
  • Grouped median = L + ((N/2 − cf)/f) × h, where cf is the cumulative frequency before the median class.
  • Mode: most frequent value. Grouped mode = L + ((f1 − f0)/(2f1 − f0 − f2)) × h.
  • Empirical relation (moderately skewed data): Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean.

varieties.name: AM, GM, HM and combined mean
varieties.how: Pick the right formula; for combined mean, weight each group mean by its size.

example.q: Group A (30 students) has mean 40; group B (20 students) has mean 50. Find the combined mean.

varieties.name: Median, mode and the empirical relation
varieties.how: Sort before finding the median; use Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean when two of the three are given.

varieties.name: Grouped median and mode
varieties.how: Build the cumulative frequency column, locate the median (N/2) or modal (highest f) class, then apply the formula.

example.q: Median class 40–50, N = 60, cf before it = 22, f = 16. Find the median.

tips: For two numbers a and b: AM = (a+b)/2, GM = √(ab), HM = 2ab/(a+b).
Median is not affected by extreme values; the mean is.
In a symmetric distribution, mean = median = mode.
traps: Always sort the data before picking the median.
In the grouped median formula, cf is the cumulative frequency of the class BEFORE the median class.
GM is zero or undefined if any value is zero or negative.

questions.q: The arithmetic mean of 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 is:

questions.solution: Sorted: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. n = 6 (even), so median = average of 3rd and 4th values = (7 + 9)/2 = 8.
